picks.title: Replacing creative jobs with AI could have a hidden cost, a new report warns
picks.excerpt: D&AD's 2026 AI and Creativity Report finds AI-declared award entries more than doubled year-on-year to 27.6%, while studios quietly cut the junior, repetitive work AI now absorbs. The warning: those tasks are where creative judgement was traditionally trained, so automating them may starve the next generation of design leads.
picks.rationale: Hard numbers from D&AD on how fast AI entered award-winning work, plus the staffing consequence studios are walking into without noticing.

picks.title: Block's new Apache 2.0 agent workspace Berd works across models and harnesses, stores conversation history locally
picks.excerpt: Block open-sourced Berd, a free desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that gives AI agents roles, skills, tools and recognizable visual identities via personas like Berdy, Pushback and Copycat. A rare look at what deliberate agent-identity design looks like as a shipped product.
picks.rationale: A free, open-source agent workspace you can install today, and the clearest shipped example yet of designing agents as characters rather than chat boxes.

picks.title: Why AI Should Return Interfaces, Not Walls of Text
picks.excerpt: Argues that the chat-first default — ask for an outcome, get a wall of prose — is a design failure, and that AI responses should render actual components. A concrete case for generative UI over generative text.
picks.rationale: Reframes the AI response itself as a design surface: if the model can return components, the designer owns the output instead of the prompt box.

picks.title: Scantic trains 3D Gaussian Splats entirely on your phone
picks.excerpt: A new free iOS app generates 3D Gaussian Splat scans of objects and environments entirely on-device, with no cloud processing. Puts neural-radiance-style capture in a designer's pocket for reference, previz and product scanning.
picks.rationale: Splat training moves from a GPU rig to a phone with no cloud round-trip — the lowest-friction way yet to get a real object into a 3D scene.

picks.title: Humans-in-the-loop is likely the fastest way to AI value
picks.excerpt: The more valuable and complex a design or manufacturing process becomes, the more it matters to define exactly where the machine stops and the person takes over. A practical framework for drawing the handoff line in AI-assisted product development.
picks.rationale: Gives design and product teams a concrete way to draw the machine-to-human handoff line instead of handing an agent the whole process.
